`gcamsdg` covers two steps: 1) extracting results for a set of scenarios from a GCAM database, and 2) post-processing those results, combined with external datasets and tools, into SDG-specific indicators. Both steps happen through a single function, `run()`. This tutorial walks through its main modes: a single database ([Example 1](#example1)), several separate policy-scenario databases diffed against a baseline ([Example 2](#example2)), submitting the same call as a SLURM job on the BC3 cluster ([Example 3](#example3)), pairing it with a standard gcamreport run ([Example 4](#example4)), and generating basic figures ([Example 5](#example5)).

To see the full parameter list, run `?run`, or look at the [reference index](https://bc3lc.github.io/gcamsdg/reference/index.html). [debug_template.R](https://github.com/bc3LC/gcamsdg/blob/main/debug_template.R) runs every example below against a real database in one script for offline testing - copy it to `debug.R` (gitignored, so your local paths never get committed), fill in the `CONFIG` section, and run. Its section numbers match the example numbers here 1:1.

<span style="color:white">newline</span>


## Example 1: compute SDG indicators for a single GCAM database {#example1}

1) Install the package (see the [README](https://github.com/bc3LC/gcamsdg#installation)):

``` r
devtools::install_github("bc3LC/gcamsdg")
```

2) Load it. If you are using RStudio or working directly on a clone, run

``` r
devtools::load_all()
```

and otherwise

``` r
library(gcamsdg)
```

3) Call `run()` with your database. `db_path` defaults to `<base_path>/output`, and `base_path` defaults to the BC3 "DIPC" cluster path - pass your own for a local run or a different cluster/machine:

``` r
result <- run(
  db_name = "my_gcam_database",       # extension added automatically if missing
  base_path = "/path/to/your/GCAM_run_dir",
  desired_scen = c("scen1", "scen2"), # omit to use every scenario in the database
  sdgs = "all"                        # or e.g. c("gdp", "water") to skip the rest
)
```

Behind the scenes this creates (or, on a later call, loads) an rgcam project via `create_prj()` - which reads all the SDG queries bundled with the package (`inst/extdata/queries_*.xml`) plus a couple of heavier queries added only when needed (detailed land allocation for `"land"`, nonCO2 emissions for `"health"`) - then computes each requested indicator.

4) Check the result: `result` is a named list, one data frame per requested SDG (`result$gdp`, `result$water`, ...). Each indicator's raw CSV output is also written under `gcamsdg/output/<SDG>/indiv_results/` (one subfolder per SDG: `SDG0-POP`, `SDG1-GDP`, `SDG1-Expenditure`, `SDG2-Poverty`, `SDG3-Health`, `SDG6-Water`, `SDG15-Land`).

**SDG 1's expenditure indicator** compares each scenario's income against a baseline (REF) scenario's, so it needs `ssp` and a baseline project (`prj_base`) - if you set `base_scen` (see [Example 2](#example2)) and the baseline happens to be one of the databases you're already processing, `run()` finds it automatically; otherwise pass `prj_base` yourself:

``` r
prj_base <- load_prj("prj_files", "my_baseline_database.dat")
result <- run(db_name = "my_gcam_database", base_path = "...",
              sdgs = "expenditure", ssp = "SSP2", prj_base = prj_base)
```

**SDG 15** additionally downscales GCAM land allocation with [Demeter](https://github.com/JGCRI/demeter) via `reticulate`, so it needs a conda environment with Demeter installed (`conda_env`, defaults to the BC3 cluster's):

``` r
result <- run(db_name = "my_gcam_database", base_path = "...",
              sdgs = "land", conda_env = "/path/to/your/demeter-conda-env")
```

<span style="color:white">newline</span>


## Example 2: several policy-scenario databases, diffed against a baseline {#example2}

Real mitigation-scenario ensembles often split each policy scenario into its own separate GCAM database. Pass a vector to `db_name` (and, optionally, `prj_name` to control the saved project names) - `run()` extracts/loads each one, computes the requested `sdgs` for all of them, and combines the results before anything else happens:

``` r
result <- run(
  db_name = c("database_basexdb_policyA", "database_basexdb_policyB", "database_basexdb_base"),
  base_path = "/path/to/your/GCAM_run_dir",
  sdgs = "all",
  show_diff = TRUE,
  base_scen = "myBaselineScenario"
)
```

With `show_diff = TRUE`, each returned indicator is averaged over the model period, diffed against `base_scen`, tagged by policy sector (afolu/ind/bld/trn/dac/sup, inferred from the scenario name), and pivoted wide - the same table `run_comparisson()` used to produce, now built in directly. Without `show_diff`, you get the raw per-scenario values instead (as in [Example 1](#example1), just combined across every database in `db_name`).

<span style="color:white">newline</span>


## Example 3: running on the BC3 cluster {#example3}

Set `cluster = TRUE` to submit the exact same call as a SLURM job instead of running it locally:

``` r
job <- run(
  db_name = c("database_basexdb_policyA", "database_basexdb_policyB", "database_basexdb_base"),
  sdgs = "all", show_diff = TRUE, base_scen = "myBaselineScenario",
  cluster = TRUE
)
job$job_id      # SLURM job ID
job$log_file    # where to check progress/errors
job$output_path # where results will land once the job completes
```

This fills in the bundled sbatch template ([inst/extdata/gcamsdg_cluster.sbatch](https://github.com/bc3LC/gcamsdg/blob/main/inst/extdata/gcamsdg_cluster.sbatch)) with the call's arguments and submits it via `sbatch`. It's **fire-and-forget**: `run()` returns the job ID immediately rather than waiting for the SLURM job to finish, since that happens later, asynchronously, on a compute node. Check on it the normal SLURM way (`squeue`, the returned log file) and read the results from `job$output_path` once it's done.

Before your first cluster run, edit the `#SBATCH` directives at the top of the bundled template once for your own account/partition/resource needs, or override individual ones per call without touching the file:

``` r
run(db_name = "...", cluster = TRUE, sbatch_args = list(time = "48:00:00", mem = "64G"))
```

`cluster = TRUE` only works with the `db_path`+`db_name` or existing-`prj_name`-file input modes - an in-memory `prj` object can't be handed to a job running on a different node.

<span style="color:white">newline</span>


## Example 4: also producing the standard gcamreport output {#example4}

If you also want the standard [gcamreport](https://github.com/bc3LC/gcamreport) IPCC-style output from the same project (instead of extracting the database a second time), set `run_gcamreport = TRUE` and provide `GCAM_version`:

``` r
result <- run(
  db_name = "my_gcam_database", base_path = "/path/to/your/GCAM_run_dir",
  sdgs = "all",
  run_gcamreport = TRUE, GCAM_version = "v7.1"
)
result$gcamreport  # gcamreport's standardized output
```

This requires the `gcamreport` package (`devtools::install_github("bc3LC/gcamreport")`) and, currently, a single database/project (not a vector `db_name`).

<span style="color:white">newline</span>


## Example 5: basic figures {#example5}

Set `makeFigures = TRUE` to also generate a basic PNG per computed indicator:

``` r
result <- run(
  db_name = "my_gcam_database", base_path = "/path/to/your/GCAM_run_dir",
  sdgs = c("gdp", "poverty", "water"),
  makeFigures = TRUE
)
```

Each PNG is saved alongside that indicator's other output, under `gcamsdg/output/<SDG>/figures/` (e.g. `.../SDG1-GDP/figures/gdp.png`) - a scenario-colored time series line chart for indicators with a year dimension, or a bar chart by scenario for SDG15's PSL (a single net 2020-2050 value, no year dimension). Regional indicators (population, GDP, health) are aggregated to one global series first - GDP uses an unweighted regional average for this quick chart (a real population-weighted GDP per capita is what `show_diff`'s diff-vs-baseline step computes instead).

This does **not** produce geographic maps (e.g. water scarcity by basin, PSL by ecoregion) - the underlying indicator functions currently aggregate that spatial detail away before returning their result, so real choropleth maps would need a deeper change to what they return, not just a plotting helper.
